name: Kolsass
kurzbeschreibung: Cozy village in the Unterinntal between Wattens and Schwaz, featuring a Baroque church and excellent transport links.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kolsass is a historic village in the Tyrolean Unterinntal valley, located approximately 20 kilometres east of the provincial capital Innsbruck. Situated at an altitude of 553 metres on a gentle alluvial terrace south of the Inn River, the municipality rests at the opening of the Kolsassbach valley at the northern foot of the Tux Prealps. With a population of around 1,650 residents, Kolsass offers a pleasant combination of rural serenity, rich historical heritage, and swift access to the cultural and commercial hubs of the Hall-Wattens region. The prominent ruins of Neu-Rettenberg Castle and longstanding artisanal traditions define the character of this authentic Tyrolean settlement.

History

Kolsass stands among the oldest continuously settled sites in the central Inn Valley. Its name stems from pre-Roman Rhaetian origins and was first documented around 1050 as Cholsass. During the High Middle Ages, it served as an important mother parish for surrounding settlements. The town achieved notable prominence around 1500 through Florian Waldauf von Waldenstein, a trusted confidant and councilor to Emperor Maximilian I. Waldauf acquired Castle Rettenberg above the village, expanding it into a splendid residence and establishing significant religious foundations. Copper and silver were mined in the Kolsass valley for centuries, with gold panning along the stream. The baroque parish church of the Visitation features exquisite ceiling frescoes by master Wolfram Köberl.

Getting There

Kolsass benefits from prime transport links across the Inntal transit corridor. By car, the village is easily accessed from the A12 Inntal Autobahn via the Wattens exit to the west or the Vomp exit to the east, connecting via the B171 federal road. Rail passengers use the Tyrolean S-Bahn suburban network (lines S4 and S5), with the Fritzens-Kolsass station located just a short walk north of the village across the Inn River, providing frequent direct trains to Innsbruck, Jenbach, and Kufstein. The scenic Inn Cycle Path also runs directly along the municipal border.

Tips

A rewarding walking tour ascends from the village centre to the ruins of Neu-Rettenberg Castle, the historic site of the annual Miners' Florian Festival offering panoramic views across the Inn Valley. Culture enthusiasts should explore the parish church of the Visitation to admire its celebrated baroque ceiling frescoes. Nature lovers will enjoy tranquil paths along the rushing Kolsassbach stream, exploring sites connected to historical ore mining and gold panning. In addition, the internationally renowned Swarovski Crystal Worlds in neighbouring Wattens are just a short bicycle ride or bus trip away.
